# Decompose the `worklist.ts` god class

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — 7,823 lines, 89 exported symbols,
20 banner-delimited sections, one 2,260-line function (`runWorklistTui`, 5564–7823).

## Problem statement

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` carries the entire Herdr work-item selection
experience — constants and maps, the mutable list state machine, row/detail/meta
formatting, tooltip and help rendering, chord and key handling, the mouse input
pipeline, the list renderer, command dispatch and the TUI lifecycle loop — in a
single 7,823-line module. Because the biggest single concern (`runWorklistTui`,
2,260 lines of nested closures over one large mutable context) sits in the same
file as everything else, every change requires holding thousands of unrelated
lines in view, and the blast radius of a diff is not legible from the file it
touches.

This item is the follow-up filed by WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (producer directive,
intake Q1 → A: *"If any file is >1000 lines it should be evaluated for
refactoring and if appropriate a work item should be created"*). The
downtime-worker decomposition established the pattern this item reuses:
move-only extraction, thin compatibility barrel, tests untouched as the
behaviour gate, sequenced child items.

## Users

- **Herdr UI maintainers (agents and humans)** changing one concern (a key
  binding, the metadata panel, the mouse drag path, the refresh loop) without
  re-reading 7,800 lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** who need a diff whose blast radius is attributable to
  one module and one test file.
- **Future agents** implementing worklist work items, who need named modules
  locatable by file search instead of a monolith.
- **Operators** who benefit indirectly: smaller modules shorten the review and
  audit cycle for every worklist change.

Example user stories:

- As an agent changing the metadata panel, I want `formatMetadataPanel` and its
  helpers in their own module so that I can verify the change against its own
  tests.
- As a reviewer, I want the key-handling diff to touch only the key-handling
  module so that I can reason about input regressions in isolation.
- As a maintainer, I want every module under 1,000 lines so that any one concern
  is readable in a single pass.
- As a maintainer, I want `runWorklistTui` to be a thin orchestrator over named
  handler modules so that the TUI lifecycle is reviewable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No production file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports
   ≤1,000 for `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (reduced to a thin barrel) and for
   every module created by the split. The single 2,260-line `runWorklistTui`
   function is broken up so no module and no single exported function carries it
   whole.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./worklist.js` by another module remains exported from that
   exact path with identical types and values, so the 34 importing files
   (2 production consumers + 32 test files, of which 22 are `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites) compile with no import-path edits. 66 distinct symbols are imported
   today; the barrel
   re-exports **only symbols consumers actually use** — unused exports stay
   internal to the extracted modules (inherited producer decision, parent
   WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 intake Q2 → "A, but only re-export symbols that are
   actually used").
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change,
   no renames of public symbols, no behavioural diffs. No test file is modified —
   not its import paths, fixtures or assertions — and all 22 `worklist*.test.ts`
   suites (15,433 lines) plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `worklist.js` barrel or from `index.ts`; the
   existing `worklist → fetcher/visibility/…` edge direction is preserved and no
   new cycle is introduced.
5. **State ownership is explicit and singular.** The mutable
   `WorkItemListState` (848-line section) and the TUI-local mutable context
   currently closed over by `runWorklistTui` each live in exactly one module;
   extraction must not duplicate mutable state or fork the source of truth.
6. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners such as
   `// ── Mouse / touch input (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ) ──`) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
7. **Testing/validation criterion:** the extracted modules are covered by the
   existing, unmodified `worklist*.test.ts` suites; the split adds no behaviour
   of its own, so no new assertions are required. Validation includes
   `tsc --noEmit`/build success, no new circular-import report, and a line-count
   check asserting every `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` production module is
   ≤1,000 lines.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and rewire imports; do not refactor logic,
  improve naming, or "fix" anything encountered on the way (record such findings
  as new work items instead).
- **Barrel compatibility.** 34 files import from `./worklist.js` or
  `./worklist` (including 22 `worklist*.test.ts` suites and the production
  consumers `index.ts` and `fetcher.ts`). The barrel preserves that contract.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first (constants,
  types, layout, formatting) and work inwards towards the state machine and the
  TUI loop, so each merged step leaves the build and the full suite green.
- **`runWorklistTui` is the hard part.** Its 2,260 lines are nested closures
  sharing one large mutable context. The extraction must keep a single context
  object (interface-typed, owned by one module) and pass it explicitly to
  extracted handler functions rather than duplicating state or converting to a
  class-based controller (that would be a behavioural rewrite, not a move).
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to Herdr
  key bindings, shortcuts, rendering output or the `wl` CLI contract.
- **Scope boundary.** This epic targets production modules under
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts`. Test files exceeding the ceiling
  (`worklist.test.ts` 7,073 lines, `worklist-mouse.test.ts` 1,132 lines) are
  **out of scope** under the recommended option (see Appendix Q1) and would be
  filed as a follow-up item, because splitting them would violate AC3
  (unmodified tests as the behaviour gate).
- **Other >1,000-line herdr files are out of scope** (tracked separately:
  `index.ts` WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6, `fetcher.ts` WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1,
  `dispatcher-anchor.ts` WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ, `downtime-log.ts`
  WL-0MVGKHFT4003X6JW, `downtime-worker.ts` WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7).

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` is 7,823 lines, 89 exports, 20 sections (line
ranges from the current `dev` checkout):

Structural facts discovered during intake:

- **66 of 89 exports are imported elsewhere.** Most-imported:
  `runWorklistTui` (21 files), `WorkItemListState` (9), `ANSI` (6),
  `formatItemLine` (5), `handleKeypress` (5), `formatDetailContent` (4),
  `createListRenderer` (4), `formatMetadataPanel` (3), `mapMouseToAction` (3),
  `buildMetaRows` (3). The remaining 23 exports are unused outside the module
  and become internal per AC2.
- **Non-test consumers are only two files:** `index.ts`
  (`runWorklistTui`, `getTermSize`) and `fetcher.ts` (`STAGES`, type `Stage`).
  Everything else importing is a test.
- **`runWorklistTui` internal concerns** (from its nested-function scan):
  pane markers and event subscriptions (5606–6141), metadata blocker resolution
  (5654–5803), refresh/sync/dispatch (6143–6480), key input (6484–7172),
  stdin decode + key-file IO + help entries (7173–7274), render (7275–7504),
  resize + scheduler + hydrator + resume poll (7505–7823). These are the natural
  extraction seams for the loop.
- **Dependency direction:** `worklist.ts` imports from `fetcher`, `visibility`,
  `pane-title`, `events`, `agent-tracker`, `code-freeze`, `ship-guard`,
  `shortcut-config`, `auto-sync`, `scheduler`, `settings`, `db-change`,
  `downtime-worker`, `downtime-log`, `dispatch-view`, `hydrator`, `notify`,
  `command-log`, `form-dialog`, `clipboard`, `ship-it-dialog`, `key-input`,
  `grouping`, `md-viewer`, `md-note-edit` and `@worklog/shared/icons`. Nothing
  outside imports the individual UI internals, so the extracted modules have a
  clean one-way boundary to preserve.
- **Precedent:** WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (downtime-worker.ts, 8,105 → thin barrel,
  sequenced child items) and WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO (`src/database.ts`, 2,584
  lines, completed) used the same AC shape: unchanged public API, tests pass
  unmodified, per-module line ceiling.

## Desired change

Reduce `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` to a thin re-export barrel and move its

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — reduce to a re-export barrel; preserve every consumed export.

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.keys.ts` — new; key mapping and keypress handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.mouse.ts` — new; mouse/touch parse-map-dispatch pipeline.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.render.ts` — new; list renderer and status/banner fragments.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.commands.ts` — new; command resolution, dispatch and dialogs.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-context.ts`, `worklist.tui-handlers.ts`, `worklist.tui-input.ts`, `worklist.tui-render.ts` — new; extracted TUI loop concerns.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — verify unchanged (barrel keeps them compiling as-is).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.test.ts` — must remain unmodified; they are the behaviour-preservation gate.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr package overview (worklist behaviour reference).
- `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` — references `worklist.ts` `formatItemLine` and `worklist.test.ts` colour tests; update the file references if module names change.
- `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/herdr-events-subscribe-reliability.md`, `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md`, `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — reference `worklist.ts` by path; verify the references still resolve.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — `runWorklistTui` closure extraction (high).** 2,260 lines of closures
  over shared mutable state; moving them behind an explicit context risks
  behavioural drift in refresh/scheduler/resume-poll ordering. *Mitigation:*
  extract one closure group per child item, keep the context interface-typed and
  single-owner, land each step with the full suite green, and treat
  `worklist*.test.ts` as the gate.
- **Risk — silent re-export drift (medium).** Trimming the barrel to used
  symbols only can break a consumer the search missed (dynamic imports, tests
  using `import *`). *Mitigation:* derive the used-symbol set mechanically from
  the import scan, then verify with `tsc --noEmit` across the package.
- **Risk — cycle formation (medium).** Extracted modules that need shared types
  may reach for `worklist.js` or `index.ts`. *Mitigation:* put shared types in
  `worklist.types.ts` (leaf), and forbid barrel imports from extracted modules
  (AC4), verified by the dependency check.
- **Risk — review fatigue / large diff (medium).** A single big-bang split would
  be unreviewable. *Mitigation:* sequenced child items, leaf-first, one concern
  per child.
- **Risk — scope creep (medium).** The split will surface dead code, duplicated
  helpers and naming oddities. *Mitigation:* record them as new work items;
  do not fix in place.
- **Assumption — test files are out of scope** for the ceiling in this epic
  (Appendix Q1 recommended option A): tests stay unmodified as the behaviour
  gate and the two oversized suites (`worklist.test.ts` 7,073,
  `worklist-mouse.test.ts` 1,132) get a dedicated follow-up item.
- **Assumption — inherited producer decisions** from WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 apply
  unchanged: barrel re-exports used symbols only (Q2), and the epic is delivered
  as sequenced child items in dependency order, one per extracted module (Q3).
- **Assumption — no public API beyond `./worklist.js`** is promised: the
  extracted module paths are internal to `packages/herdr`.

## Decompose the `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` god module

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (2,935 lines, 37 exported symbols)

## Problem statement

`packages/herdr/src/index.ts` is the Herdr plugin entry point and has grown to
2,935 lines. It currently carries command routing, argument builders, background
dispatch, pane-ID capture, claim/priority resolution, interactive window and tab
placement, pane cleanup, dozens of production dependency resolvers, the
downtime-worker dependency factory, settings bootstrap and the full TUI
`main()` loop in one module. Navigating, reviewing and safely changing any one
concern requires holding the whole file in view, so every dispatch or TUI change
carries avoidable regression risk.

The 1,000-line maintainability ceiling was adopted for the parent refactor
series WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7. This item is the `index.ts` member of that sweep and
was created specifically to bring this file under the ceiling.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one concern
  (e.g. background dispatch, interactive placement, the TUI loop) without
  reasoning about 2,800 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need a focused diff whose blast radius is legible from
  the touched module.
- **Future agents implementing plugin work items** need small, named modules
  they can locate with a file search instead of reading a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent implementing a background-dispatch change, I want that path in a
  dedicated module so I can modify it without re-reading the TUI loop.
- As a reviewer, I want a split diff attributable to a single concern so I can
  verify it against its own tests.
- As a maintainer, I want each module under 1,000 lines so a file is readable in
  a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (now a thin barrel/entry module) and for every module created by the split.

## Refactor: decompose src/github.ts god class (goal: no file > 1000 lines)

**File:** `src/github.ts` (1,755 lines, 58 public exports)

## Problem statement

`src/github.ts` exceeds the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (downtime-worker.ts decomposition). It concentrates GitHub
CLI transport, retry/backoff, label management, marker parsing, sub-issue
hierarchy, comments, issue CRUD and assignment in one module, making
navigation, review and safe change harder than needed.

## Goal

Break the file into cohesive modules so no file exceeds 1,000 lines, while
keeping the public API importable unchanged from `src/github.ts` (barrel).
Producer directive (WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 intake Q1, answered): every source file
over 1,000 lines should be evaluated for refactoring and, where appropriate,
decomposed.

## Users

- **Maintainers/reviewers** of the GitHub integration — want cohesive modules
  with single responsibilities so a change to one concern (e.g. label logic)
  does not require hunting through 1,700 lines.
- **Agents implementing sibling god-class items** (sync.ts, persistent-store.ts,
  github-sync.ts) — this decomposition is the first in the series to land for
  the GitHub surface; its barrel + invariant-test pattern is the template.
- **Test suite / CI** — must stay green with zero test-file edits.

User stories:

- As a maintainer, I want to find the `gh` CLI transport code without scanning a
  1,700-line file, so changes to retry/backoff behaviour are localised.
- As a reviewer of a future label-handling change, I want label code confined to
  one module, so behaviour-preserving proofs are tractable.
- As a CI bot, I want a cheap regression guard asserting the split invariants,
  so a regrowth or an accidental public-API change fails the build.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **File-size ceiling.** Every file produced by the split — the `src/github.ts`
   barrel and each new module — is under 1,000 lines (measured with `wc -l`;
   largest predicted module ≈ 470 lines). Target: no file in the GitHub
   integration exceeds the ceiling.
2. **Unchanged public API.** `src/github.ts` re-exports exactly the same public
   names as today (the 58 exports listed in `Existing state` — no additions, no
   removals, no renames), so all consumers importing from
   `./github.js` / `../src/github.js` compile unchanged. Verified by a new
   structure test comparing the barrel's export surface against the
   pre-refactor list.
3. **Move-only, test-preserving.** No existing test file is modified (no import
   path or assertion changes) and the full existing GitHub test suite passes
   via the test skill. Existing `vi.mock('../src/github.js')` factories
   (full-replacement and `importOriginal` styles) keep working.
4. **No new circular imports.** No extracted module imports from
   `./github.js` (barrel); dependency direction is strictly
   `github.ts` → submodules → (github-types.ts, github-transport.ts), with the
   optional `github-throttler.js` consumers unchanged. Verified by a structure
   test (module-graph check) and by the TypeScript build.
5. **Documentation and full suite.** Module responsibilities documented (JSDoc
   header per module + a "GitHub module layout" note in
   `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`); references to code locations updated in
   `docs/github-throttling.md` and `docs/SHELL_ESCAPING.md`; the full project
   test suite passes.

## Constraints

- All consumers keep importing from `src/github.ts` — do **not** repoint any
  consumer (e.g. `github-sync.ts`, `delegate-helper.ts`, `commands/github.ts`,
  `jsonl.ts`) to submodules. Some tests replace the whole
  `../src/github.js` module with a mock factory (e.g.
  `tests/github-sync-comments.test.ts`, `tests/cli/delegate-guard-rails.test.ts`),
  so the barrel is the single import surface.
- Extracted modules may not import from the barrel (cycle guard); the shared
  `setVerboseLogger` state lives in the transport module and stays a singleton
  (ESM module instance) reachable via the barrel.
- Behaviour-preserving: no logic, signature, or export-name changes; no new
  runtime dependencies.
- New module filenames must not collide with existing
  `src/github-sync.ts`, `src/github-throttler.ts`, `src/github-metrics.ts`,
  `src/github-pre-filter.ts`, `src/lib/github-helper.ts`.

- **Singleton state risk (low):** `setVerboseLogger` moves to the transport

- **Scope-creep risk:** do not fix or refactor logic while moving (e.g.
  deprecated `ensureGithubLabels` stays deprecated and private); record any
  improvement opportunity as a new work item, not scope.
- **Failure mode:** a barrel that re-exports a name twice (or a module that
  exports the same name as another) yields ambiguous `export *` errors — use
  explicit named re-exports in `src/github.ts`, not `export *`.
- **Estimate caveat:** module line estimates (sum ≈ 1,865) exceed today's 1,755

- **Assumption:** flat `src/github-*.ts` naming is acceptable (repo

- Q: Is there an existing regression guard to reuse? — Answer (agent

# Refactor: decompose `src/commands/interview.ts` god class

**File:** `src/commands/interview.ts` — 1,630 lines, 41 exports, 9 logical sections.

## Problem statement

`src/commands/interview.ts` carries the whole `wl interview` backend — clarifying-section
detection, Q/A parsing and lossless re-serialisation, the producer-review explanation
(LLM + structured fallback), LLM-assisted question extraction, the interactive walkthrough
loop, readline plumbing and Commander registration — in one 1,630-line module. It breaches
the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7, so navigating,
reviewing and safely changing any one concern means holding the whole file in view.

## Users

- **Agents implementing interview/LLM changes** — need one concern (e.g. the answer
  re-serialiser, or the extraction prompt) locatable by file search instead of by reading
  1,630 lines; a monolith inflates context cost and increases the chance of editing the
  wrong helper with a similar name (`cleanQuestion` vs `firstLine` vs `truncateBytes`).
- **Reviewers/auditors** — need a diff whose blast radius is legible from the touched
  module boundary.
- **Producers running `wl interview`** — benefit indirectly: behaviour-preserving
  decomposition lowers the regression risk of every future change to the command.

Example user stories:

- As an agent fixing a Q/A parsing defect, I want the parser and re-serialiser in one
  focused module, so that I can reason about round-trip losslessness without loading the
  LLM and Commander code.
- As a reviewer, I want each extracted module to state one responsibility, so that I can
  judge a diff against a single boundary.
- As a maintainer, I want the `wl interview` command behaviour and the public module
  surface unchanged, so that no test, registry entry or documented flag needs reworking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ceiling met.** `src/commands/interview.ts` and every file under `src/interview/` is
   ≤ 1,000 lines (target: largest extracted module ≤ 500). Evidence recorded in the work
   item as `wc -l` output for the module family.
2. **Public surface unchanged.** All 41 current exports of `src/commands/interview.ts`
   (2 section, 4 Q/A, 15 explanation, 11 extraction, 5 loop, 4 registration) plus the
   default `register` export remain importable from the unchanged specifier
   `src/commands/interview.js` with identical names, kinds and signatures; the barrel
   re-exports the full surface. `src/command-registry.ts`
   (`interview: () => import('./commands/interview.js')`) is untouched and needs no edit.
3. **Move-only, behaviour-preserving.** No logic, regex, message, ordering or flag
   changes. Test assertions, fixtures, `describe` titles and mock targets are unmodified;
   the only mechanical test change permitted is the lockstep split of the oversized suite
   `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` (1,696 lines): every resulting file is ≤ 1,000 lines,
   `describe` groups move verbatim and only import paths change. Test count is preserved
   (the split neither adds nor drops a test).
4. **No circular imports, one direction only.** Extracted modules import concrete siblings
   and `../lib/*`, `../config.js`, `../types.js`; **no** `src/interview/*` module imports
   the `src/commands/interview.ts` barrel. The dependency direction is
   `commands/interview.ts` → `interview/*`.
5. **Responsibilities documented.** Every new module carries a one-line module doc comment
   naming its single responsibility, and existing provenance comments/work-item ids
   (`WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67`, `WL-0MUUAMP7M008Z4GK`, `WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF`,
   `WL-0MUX2W8IN005RW66`, `WL-0MUQ0VP800068DNX`) move with their code.
6. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build` (tsc, NodeNext, `rootDir: src`) is green and the
   full project test suite passes via `/skill:test`.
7. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes, including
   code comments, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (command/module map), `CLI.md` if any wording
   drifts, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded
   (release pipeline).

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports only. No "while we're here" rewrites, no
  renames of public symbols, no regex or prompt-text edits. Any incidental improvement
  found en route becomes a separate `discovered-from` work item.
- **Layout: mirror `src/doctor/`.** Helpers for a single command live in a top-level
  feature directory (`src/doctor/*` ← `src/commands/doctor.ts`); this item follows that
  established precedent with `src/interview/*`. The entry file stays
  `src/commands/interview.ts` so the ESM specifier `./commands/interview.js` keeps
  resolving to `dist/commands/interview.js` under NodeNext (a directory-index barrel
  `interview/index.ts` would break that specifier).
- **No new dependencies.** Only existing imports (`../lib/llm.js`,
  `../lib/progress-feedback.js`, `../config.js`, `../mutation-lock.js`, `../types.js`,
  `../cli-types.js`, `readline`) may be used by the extracted modules.
- **No behaviour-parity tooling in scope.** A repo-wide 1,000-line guard is a separate
  open item (WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL, `discovered-from` the sweep); this item verifies the
  ceiling with `wc -l` evidence plus a small structural assertion (see Risks).
- **Escaped backticks** only in written content; Markdown otherwise.

## Existing state

`src/commands/interview.ts` — 1,630 lines, 41 exports, single default `register`, no
module-level mutable state (only `const` regexes/constants). Section map (current `dev`):

| Lines | Section | Exports |
|---|---|---|
| 1–70 | File doc comment + imports | — |
| 71–116 | Section markers (regexes, `INSERT_WRAPPER`) | — (all private) |
| 117–160 | Section extraction | `ClarifyingSection`, `extractClarifyingSection` |
| 161–564 | Q/A parsing and re-serialisation | `ClarifyingQAPair`, `parseQAPairs`, `rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription` |
| 565–873 | Producer-review explanation | 15 (caps, context/deps types, prompt, render, fallback, LLM result) |
| 874–1052 | LLM-assisted question extraction | 11 (instruction, caps, prompt, parser, result, extract fns, section insert/merge) |
| 1053–1260 | Core interview loop | `InterviewStore`, `InterviewIO`, `InterviewOutcome`, `InterviewRunOptions`, `runInterview` |
| 1261–1291 | Interactive input | — (`createPromptLoop` private) |
| 1292–1630 | Types + command registration | `InterviewPromptLoop`, `InterviewCommandDeps`, `defaultClearPrompt`, `register` (default) |

Consumers: exactly one production importer — `src/command-registry.ts` (dynamic import,
default export only) — and one test file, `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` (1,696 lines, 19
top-level `describe` blocks, no `vi.mock`, imports 11 named exports + default). No file in
`src/`, `packages/`, `scripts/` or `bench/` imports any other symbol from the module, and
no documentation references the file path.

## Desired change

Extract cohesive modules under `src/interview/`, leaving `src/commands/interview.ts` as the
command entry (registration + interactive plumbing) **and** the public barrel. Proposed map
(export attribution is exhaustive — every current export belongs to exactly one row):

| Module | Responsibility | Exports moved | Est. lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/commands/interview.ts` (entry + barrel) | Commander registration, `register` action flow, prompt loop, deps surface, re-export of the full public surface | `InterviewPromptLoop`, `InterviewCommandDeps`, `defaultClearPrompt`, `register` (default) + all re-exports | ~400 |
| `src/interview/section.ts` | Clarifying-section heading detection and extraction | `ClarifyingSection`, `extractClarifyingSection` | ~95 |
| `src/interview/qa.ts` | Q/A parsing, answer-region computation and lossless re-serialisation | `ClarifyingQAPair`, `parseQAPairs`, `rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription` | ~400 |
| `src/interview/explanation.ts` | Producer-review explanation: evidence formatting, prompt, render, structured fallback, LLM call | 15 exports | ~310 |
| `src/interview/extraction.ts` | LLM-assisted question extraction plus canonical-section insert/merge | 11 exports | ~200 |
| `src/interview/loop.ts` | Interactive walkthrough: prompt/persist answers, outcome accounting | `InterviewStore`, `InterviewIO`, `InterviewOutcome`, `InterviewRunOptions`, `runInterview` | ~220 |

Dependency direction after extraction:
`commands/interview.ts` → {section, qa, explanation, extraction, loop} →
{`../lib/llm.js`, `../lib/progress-feedback.js`, `../config.js`, `../types.js`} and
sibling modules only. `loop.ts` → `section.ts`, `qa.ts`, `extraction.ts`;
`extraction.ts` → `qa.ts`, `section.ts`. No module imports the entry barrel (AC4).

### Proposed child decomposition (structural slices)

1. **Foundation** — create `src/interview/` and extract `section.ts` + `qa.ts` (the pure,
   dependency-free parsing core). Blocks the rest.
2. **`explanation.ts`** — largest LLM cluster; independent of the loop.
3. **`extraction.ts`** — depends on `qa.ts`/`section.ts` for insert/merge helpers.
4. **`loop.ts`** — core walkthrough; depends on slices 1 and 3.
5. **Closeout** — thin the entry barrel (`src/commands/interview.ts`), lockstep split of
   `tests/cli/interview.test.ts`, module-map documentation, `wc -l` evidence, build +
   full suite.

Slices are ordered so slice 1 blocks the rest and each slice is independently move-only and
verifiable with the changed-scope test gate.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — becomes entry + barrel; loses ~1,200 lines, keeps `register`
- `src/interview/section.ts` — new (heading detection/extraction)
- `src/interview/qa.ts` — new (parse/rebuild)
- `src/interview/explanation.ts` — new (producer-review explanation)
- `src/interview/extraction.ts` — new (LLM extraction + section insert/merge)
- `src/interview/loop.ts` — new (interactive walkthrough)
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — split in lockstep into `tests/cli/interview/*.test.ts`
  (parsing/rebuild, loop + extraction, command integration, command `--llm`/progress,
  explanation), assertions verbatim
- `src/command-registry.ts` — read-only (specifier must keep resolving)
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — command/module map note for the new `src/interview/` modules
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `docs/design/incremental-sync.md`, `CLI.md` — read-only
  unless wording names the module layout (it does not today; verify, do not churn)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Silent behaviour drift in the re-serialiser** (the lossless round-trip is the command's
  subtle core; regexes are shared between parsing and rebuild). *Mitigation:* extract
  `qa.ts` first with zero edits, keep the 19 existing `describe` groups untouched, and land
  each slice as a separate move-only commit so a regression is bisectable.
- **Barrel/ESM resolution break.** `src/commands/interview.ts` must keep existing so
  `dist/commands/interview.js` is emitted; a `interview/index.ts` barrel would silently
  break the lazy registry. *Mitigation:* AC2 + the `lazy-command-registry` and
  `entry-point-split` suites as the oracle.
- **Circular imports** if `loop.ts` or `extraction.ts` reach back into the entry for types
  or helpers. *Mitigation:* AC4 — modules import siblings and `../lib/*` only; shared types
  live with their owning module (`section.ts`, `qa.ts`, `loop.ts`).
- **Test-file split churn.** 19 `describe` groups currently share one module scope.
  *Mitigation:* move groups verbatim; add no shared helper unless two target files need the
  same fixture, and then only a mechanical extraction.
- **Regrowth repeats.** This sweep already has a "completed" decomposition that never
  landed (see Related work). *Mitigation within scope:* documented single-responsibility
  module headers; the repo-wide guard is WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL (separate, low priority).
- **Scope creep risk.** The split invites opportunistic "while we're here" cleanups — a
  parser rewrite, prompt-tuning, a new `--flag`, splitting the 266-line `register` action
  into sub-commands. *Mitigation:* AC3 forbids logic edits; any such opportunity is filed
  as a separate item linked `discovered-from:WL-0MVGKGXN80006V9P` rather than absorbed.
- **Review fatigue on a wide-but-shallow diff.** A move-only refactor touches many files
  for zero behavioural gain, which can invite under-review. *Mitigation:* one concern per
  commit/slice, `git diff --color-moved` for reviewers, and the unchanged suites as the
  behaviour oracle.
- **Assumption:** the 1,000-line ceiling applies to non-test source, and to a test file only
  when it is touched in lockstep with its module (sweep rule; identical to
  WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT AC3).
- **Assumption:** the full 41-symbol public surface is retained in the barrel rather than
  trimmed to the 12 symbols tests import. Trimming would be a breaking change for any
  external plugin consumer and buys nothing here; the barrel re-export is ~10 lines.
- **Assumption:** no consumer call-site changes are acceptable — `src/command-registry.ts`
  and the CLI help output must be byte-identical for `wl interview`.
- **Assumption:** no behavioural improvement is bundled; opportunities observed en route
  become separate `discovered-from` items.

## Related work

- WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — parent sweep/directive: every production file > 1,000 lines is
  evaluated for decomposition (producer Q1 answered).
- WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT — sibling from the same sweep (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`);
  source of the lockstep test-split rule reused in AC3 and the module-map layout pattern
  (entry façade + cohesive modules + explicit dependency direction).
- WL-0MULI1N1N0001WRD — "CLI: Explanation path & new options" (completed); introduced the
  `--no-llm`/`--json` modes and the producer-review explanation path extracted here. (The
  seed description labelled this item "Interview LLM fallback"; the title above is the
  accurate one — the LLM *extraction* fallback is WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF.)

# Investigate in-process CLI harness cost (~200 ms per invocation)

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

Timing the in-process CLI harness (`tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`,
`runInProcess()`, used by `execAsync` in `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`):

- `--help` (no DB work): ~72 ms per invocation
- `list --json`, `create`, `status`: ~196–257 ms per invocation

The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) makes roughly 1200 such
in-process invocations — about 240 s of aggregate test time across
`close-recursive` (46 tests), `issue-management` (49), `issue-status` (43),
`valid-json-output` (38) and `json-output-shape` (18), plus seeding in
`beforeEach` hooks.

Every invocation constructs a fresh `Command`, re-registers ~35 built-in
commands, loads config, opens a SQLite database (with schema/migrations) and
closes it. The suite measured 624 s → 427–547 s after WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8, and
this in-process pool is the next largest remaining aggregate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Profile one `runInProcess` call and attribute the per-call cost
  (commander registration vs config load vs DB open/close vs command action).
- Where the cost is test-harness overhead (not production behaviour being
  asserted), reduce it without changing what each test asserts — candidates:
  reusing the command/plugin-context across calls for stateless reads,
  avoiding repeated YAML config parses, sharing DB open across calls within a
  test file.
- If the cost is production CLI startup (DB schema/migrations, plugin scan),
  record the findings and re-scope: the change then belongs in `src/` and is a
  production decision, not a test-only change.
- Canonical suite stays green with unchanged test counts; median wall-clock
  on a consistent host improves versus the pre-change baseline of this item.

# Maintenance routines skill: create/maintain daily scheduled test, standup, refactor sessions at high priority

## Headline

A new ContextHub skill (`/skill:maintenance-routines`) that creates and maintains the required daily scheduled maintenance sessions (test 07:00, standup 08:00, refactor 09:00) in each project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatching all of them at **high request priority** so they are processed even in peak periods — backed by a herdr enhancement that threads a per-entry `priority` (default `high`) into the `X-Priority` request header.

## Problem statement

Every project should run regular automated maintenance routines (test suite, standup report, refactor pass). The herdr plugin already has the mechanism (`scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatched on idle by the downtime worker), but there is no maintained, canonical set: the current template/live config only carries `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (06:05, no priority), and **no** `/skill:test` routine. Worse, dispatched scheduled prompts have no work item, so they receive the downtime request-priority default `medium` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium`) — they can be starved behind peak-period contention. The operator wants the three routines scheduled daily (07:00/08:00/09:00) and dispatched at **high** priority.

## Users

- **Project operator** — wants the three routines to reliably exist in each project's schedule and to be processed even in peak periods.
- **Automated maintenance sessions** (`/skill:test`, `/skill:standup`, `/skill:refactor`) — must carry `X-Priority: high` on every provider request so `llama-proxy` serves them ahead of the contention queue.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I run `/skill:maintenance-routines` on a project and it ensures `/skill:test` (daily 07:00), `/skill:standup` (daily 08:00) and `/skill:refactor` (daily 09:00) are present and correctly configured in `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, without touching my last-run timestamps or any custom entries.
- As an operator, I know every scheduled maintenance session is dispatched with `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=high` (→ `X-Priority: high`), so the daily test/standup/refactor runs are served even during peak periods.
- As an operator, when I provision a new project with `wl init`, it comes pre-loaded with the same three routines (daily, timed, high priority).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Skill exists and reconciles the schedule.** `skill/maintenance-routines/` ships a `SKILL.md`, a reconciler script and unit tests. Invoking it (or the script directly) reconciles the project-local `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (under the resolved worklog dir) so these required routines are present and exact:
   - `/skill:test` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "07:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:standup` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "08:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:refactor` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "09:00"`, `priority: "high"`

## Problem

The downtime dispatcher's no-dispatch decision log (`<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) is capped at **100 lines** (rolling). On a busy machine that is roughly **one hour** of history, because every tick that is refused for a capacity/prefill reason writes a decision entry.

During the 2026-10-22/23 overnight starvation investigation this meant the whole night could not be reconstructed: the retained window started at `2026-10-23T05:59:58Z` and the decisions for the preceding ~8 hours had already been rotated out. The pre-05:30 reasons had to be *inferred* from pi session activity instead of read from the log.

For contrast, the retained 84-minute window carried 66 no-dispatch decisions — so the cap is genuinely exhausted in about an hour of saturated polling.

## Why it matters

- Capacity-saturation starvation is silent by design (NOP), so the decision log is the **only** forensic evidence that dispatch was attempted and why it was refused.
- Post-mortem of an overnight outage ("why did almost nothing dispatch?") is currently impossible after the fact; the operator has to guess.
- The same problem affects distinguishing `capacity-saturated` / `slots-unavailable` / `prefill-cap` / `idle-age-pending` / `no-candidate` / `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze` after rotation.

## Goal

As an operator, I want at least a full night (24 h) of downtime dispatch decisions to remain available on a busy machine, so that a post-mortem can report the actual terminal reasons and their counts, with bounded disk use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — On a machine producing decision entries at the observed rate (≥ 60/hour), at least the **last 24 hours** of `no-dispatch` decisions are readable after the fact (verified by a test that writes > 1,500 entries and asserts the oldest 24 h window is still present).
- [ ] AC2 — Disk growth is bounded: rotation happens on a documented size/time policy (e.g. daily files with a retention window, or size-based rotation with N kept), and the policy is configurable with a documented default.
- [ ] AC3 — An operator-facing, documented way exists to reconstruct a time-range summary (e.g. `wl`/herdr command, or documented `grep`/`jq` recipe over rotated files) that prints a reason tally per hour for a given night.
- [ ] AC4 — Existing readers/parsers of the single `downtime-coordination.log` path are either migrated atomically or continue to read the newest file without change; no dispatch decision is lost across a rotation boundary (test asserted).
- [ ] AC5 — Docs updated: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` log-schema/observability section names the retention policy and the summary recipe.

## Evidence (2026-10-23 investigation)

- `ContextHub/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`: 100 entries covering `2026-10-23T05:59:58.509Z` → `2026-10-23T07:13:27.061Z`.
- Reason tally in that retained window: `capacity-saturated` 29, `slots-unavailable` 29, `idle-age-pending` 4, `prefill-cap` 2, `idle-age-qualified` 2 (66 no-dispatch decisions).
- Earlier overnight window (roughly `2026-10-22T21:00Z` → `2026-10-23T05:30Z`) had no retained decision records at all.

## Notes

- Related: the starvation investigation item covering long-running panes holding local-LLM capacity.
- No production behaviour change to dispatch decisions is in scope — this is observability only.

## Summary

Add a `wl doctor prefix` subcommand that changes the configured project prefix in `.worklog/config.yaml` and renumbers every existing work item to the new prefix, preserving each item's suffix (e.g. `OSL-0MVK31VYQ007CN37` → `CC-0MVK31VYQ007CN37`). The flow must ask for confirmation before it changes anything, default to a read-only preview, and emit a machine-readable rename map.

## Motivation

Requested from the ContentCreator project (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`), whose configured prefix is `OSL` while the project is now branded `CC`. 1207 work items carry the `OSL-` prefix, and `wl doctor foreign-items` correctly classifies any item whose prefix differs from `.worklog/config.yaml` as foreign — so editing the prefix by hand would make the whole backlog look foreign and break cross-project lookups.

## Scope (proposed)

- `wl doctor prefix` — read-only preview: current prefix, counts of items/comments/dependency edges/audit records, and sample renames.
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX>` — declare the target prefix (validated: non-empty, no `-`, ASCII alphanumeric).
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX> --confirm` — apply: rewrite the config prefix, then rewrite every ID-bearing record (`workitems.id`, parent references, dependency edges, comments' `workItemId`, audit results, waivers, and any other ID column), and write a rename map (`osl→cc` pairs) to `.worklog/prefix-rename-<timestamp>.json`.
- Confirmation gate: interactive run without `--confirm` prompts and requires an explicit `y`; a non-TTY run without `--confirm` aborts with no writes and a non-zero exit.
- Idempotent: re-running after a successful rename reports a no-op.
- `--json` output for scripting.
- Docs: `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` and `CLI.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] `wl doctor prefix` (preview) reports counts and sample renames and changes nothing; covered by unit and temp-store integration tests.
- [ ] `--confirm` rewrites every ID-bearing record (items, parents, dependency edges, comments, audit results, waivers) and writes the rename map.
- [ ] Confirmation gate: non-interactive without `--confirm` aborts with a non-zero exit and zero writes; interactive requires explicit `y`.
- [ ] Re-running after a successful rename is a no-op, and a mid-run failure leaves the store recoverable (transactional or a documented rollback).
- [ ] `wl doctor foreign-items` reports zero foreign items after a confirmed rename.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (CLI.md, DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md, code comments).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

Rewriting ID references held outside the worklog store — code comments, docs, test fixtures, git commit messages, branch and worktree names. The requesting project owns that sweep and will use the rename map.

## Related

- Requested by work in the ContentCreator project (`discovered-from` recorded there).

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B (decompose the `worklist.ts` god class).

A read-only, parser-based guard that fails the build whenever a worklist
extraction step breaks one of the parent epic's structural acceptance criteria
(public surface, single state owner, no barrel/cycle regressions, module line
ceiling) — so every later child can be landed with the whole suite green and
still be structurally honest.

## Why a new test file is allowed

Parent AC3 forbids **modifying** existing tests (they are the behaviour gate).

suites byte-identical. This is the same shape the parent's precedent used:
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` +
`packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` (WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E landed first on
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7).

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts` exists and is green on the
  current tree (allowlist still containing only the monolith).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` is committed, records the
  **66 distinct consumed symbols** (the set consumers import from `./worklist.js`)
  plus reproducible provenance (source commit, generatedAt, barrel, consumer
  globs, generator command).
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` is parameterised (config object:
  barrel path, family predicate, baseline path, allowlist, single-owner
  declaration name) with the existing downtime defaults preserved so
  `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` stays green **without edits**.
- Each gate has a negative-case test proving it fails on broken input.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Public-surface gates.** The guard fails when (a) a symbol in the frozen
   baseline is no longer exported by `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, or (b) a

   declared in exactly one production module at all times.

   `./worklist.js` from any `worklist*.ts` production module, on any new
   strongly-connected component among worklist modules, and on any value-import

## Summary
Failing (red) specs that pin the parent AC2/AC3 contract: an empty own root
with a peer offer present never arms the 60-minute full-stop pause, and a
live pause is cancelled when a peer offer appears.

## Target outcome
The orchestrator suite contains one executable spec per peer-offer branch —
arming suppressed, pause cancelled by the leader's own check-in, no-peer
control case, and legacy unchanged — each failing against today's code.

## Context
Parent: WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A. The `no-candidate` probe
(orchestrator-dispatch.ts:889) checks the leader's OWN root only; when it
finds nothing it arms `cooldownUntil = now + noCandidateCooldownMs` (default
60 min) and the worker stops polling — including the coordination offer scan.
The tick's check-in block (orchestrator-tick.ts ~224-232) already cancels the
pause on a fresh OWN re-offer (WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 AC2) but never looks at
peer entries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **No 60-minute peer starvation from an empty own root.** A no-candidate
  outcome with an empty own root and one peer entry (`instanceId !== self`,
  non-empty `workItemId`) in the coordination file never arms the pause:
  `worker.paused` is false / `cooldownUntil` stays null, and the peer offer
  dispatches within one cycle (or leadership releases) — never a 60-minute
  pause (parent AC2 verification).
- A spec asserts the arming-time peer check uses the coordination entries
  already read for the dispatch — no second full worklog CLI probe.
- **Coordination check-in cancels, peer presence cancels.** The existing
  probe-before-pause is extended: with a pause already armed and a peer entry
  (non-empty `workItemId`) present, the leader's own periodic check-in
  cancels the pause on that tick (`cooldownUntil` becomes null) (parent AC3).
- A spec asserts the control case: empty own root and NO peer entry → the
  cooldown still arms exactly as today.
- A spec asserts a peer entry with `workItemId === null` neither suppresses
  arming nor cancels a live pause (only a dispatchable item counts).
- A spec asserts a self entry (`instanceId === self`) never counts as a peer
  offer.
- A spec asserts legacy mode (no `coordinationDir`) still arms the cooldown
  (parent AC4c).
- Every new spec fails against the pre-fix code; red evidence recorded in the
  completion comment.

## Minimal Implementation
- Extend packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts (cooldown
  describe) and the coordination-mode probe-before-pause describe in
  packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts; write peer entries with
  the existing `writeCoordinationFile` / `makeEntry` fixtures.
- No production code changes in this slice (test-only).

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`

- Test-first slice; runs in parallel with Feature 1. Blocks Feature 4.
